claims.subject: work:anand_historicising_2013
claims.statement: Anand questions the use of dominant historical narratives as templates for interpreting bodily difference in Indian and South Asian contexts.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only; the chapter body is unread. This critiques portability of a historiographical template, not every Western account or a single Indian consensus.

claims.subject: work:anand_historicising_2013
claims.statement: Anand compares subjects selected by existing histories of disability in India and Western scholarship to investigate how their objects of study are constituted.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only. Her sample is explicitly non-exhaustive; Usha Bhatt is a discussed predecessor, not this chapter’s coauthor.
claims.locator: Indexed publisher ABSTRACT, sample construction and Usha Bhatt discussion

claims.subject: work:bregain_handicap_2018
claims.statement: In the expanded Spanish version, Brégain investigates how organized communities and transnational transfers shape disability policies in Argentina, Brazil and Spain.
claims.qualification: Spanish introduction pp. 17–19 and 23–24 only; the book is an expanded translation of a 2018 French work. This 2022 textual witness does not establish a newly originated 2022 programme or comprehensive national coverage.
claims.locator: Spanish edition Introduction, printed pp. 17–19 and 23–24

claims.subject: work:bregain_handicap_2018
claims.statement: Brégain rejects a single continuous transition from charity to rights, attending to the coexistence and strategic use of both in historically different settings.
claims.qualification: Spanish expanded version pp. 20–21; an attributed historical interpretation, not present-day legal guidance. The first appearance of this passage in the French original is uncollated.

claims.subject: work:ferrante_prologo_2022
claims.statement: Ferrante reads Brégain’s comparative history as a resource for questioning imported disability models against Latin American histories and situated activism.
claims.qualification: A named 2022 prologue and positive reception, not independent confirmation of every book claim or evidence of a region-wide consensus. Ferrante acknowledges friendship and scholarly collaboration with Brégain.

claims.subject: work:ferrante_prologo_2022
claims.statement: Ferrante identifies language barriers to the French book’s Latin American readership and welcomes an expanded Spanish edition in open access.
claims.qualification: Her 2022 account of reception and access; not a measured readership study, a new 2022 origin for the French work, or a blanket description of Latin American language use.

claims.subject: work:consuegra_diversidad_2023
claims.statement: Consuegra Regalado identifies intellectual disability as an unevenly studied subject within Spanish disability historiography, despite a growing interdisciplinary literature.
claims.qualification: Selected Spanish introduction pp. 102–104; this is the author’s 2023 assessment of a specific historiography, not a current census or a universal founding chronology.

claims.subject: work:consuegra_diversidad_2023
claims.statement: Consuegra Regalado calls for oral and comparative history, analysis of gender, race and class, and attention to urban and rural settings while treating people with intellectual disabilities as historical actors.
claims.qualification: Selected conclusion pp. 115–116; a research programme, not evidence that its goals have been achieved. Retain the author’s Spanish terminology without imposing one universal identity label.
claims.locator: A modo de conclusión, printed pp. 115–116

claims.subject: work:nugent_border_studies_2018
claims.statement: Nugent challenges the contrast between organic European boundaries and purely imposed colonial borders, foregrounding historical processes and earlier spatial arrangements.
claims.qualification: Accepted manuscript, selected Temporality section only. An attributed comparative argument with substantial African examples; no claim that colonial coercion was absent or every border shares one genealogy.

claims.subject: work:nugent_border_studies_2018
claims.statement: Nugent distinguishes study at a boundary line from borderland zones of engagement and from bordering practices that can operate far from a physical boundary.
claims.qualification: Accepted manuscript Space section only; a particular working distinction within an interdisciplinary field, not a universal taxonomy or an equation of all border studies with history.

claims.subject: work:kaufman_mosaic_2024
claims.statement: Kaufman examines women’s captivity through later representations, colonial records and oral histories, using female–equine relations to investigate agency and erasure.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only; direct publisher body returned 403. New Spain/New Mexico case; no claim to recover every captive’s voice or represent Indigenous communities collectively.
claims.locator: Indexed primary publisher ABSTRACT, first four sentences

claims.subject: work:kaufman_mosaic_2024
claims.statement: Kaufman uses poetic annotation of Los Comanches to bring women’s sensory experiences into captivity memory while keeping archival violence and the limits of recovery visible.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only; an attributed methodological proposal, not a reconstruction of lost testimony or demonstrated reception by other historians.
claims.locator: Indexed primary publisher ABSTRACT, final two sentences

claims.subject: work:walther_mapping_2026
claims.statement: Walther reads the uneven sharing of references across one African-borderlands handbook as evidence of diverse disciplinary literatures and limited common ground.
claims.qualification: Author-institution essay analysing one forthcoming handbook, not a census of scholarship. Reported bibliometric observations were not independently reproduced; citation frequency does not establish importance or intellectual influence.
claims.locator: Web essay lines 19–28, A new handbook and A fragmented field

claims.subject: work:walther_mapping_2026
claims.statement: Walther notes that shared authorship accompanies some economic chapters’ reference overlap, whereas gender, festivals and other themes share fewer references with the common core.
claims.qualification: One editorial corpus, not a ranking of the value of themes or authors. Peripheral position is not marginal historical importance; no demographic inference from author names.

disability.label: Disability history
disability.description: Historical inquiry into disability, bodily and cognitive difference, social categories, lived experience and collective action. Medical institutions are among its subjects, alongside work, education, political life and the production of norms.
disability.scope_note: A separate research-field draft with uneven regional coverage. Disability history, disability studies, histories of medicine and the histories of particular Deaf communities overlap without being interchangeable; no single impairment or rights-movement chronology defines the field.

borderlands_history.label: Borderlands history
borderlands_history.description: Historical inquiry into border-making, contested sovereignty, mobility and communities across zones of engagement. The selected works connect spatial scale, regional knowledge, archival power and differing histories of state formation.
borderlands_history.scope_note: A separate research-field draft, distinct from a universal frontier narrative or from all transnational, imperial, Indigenous and interdisciplinary border studies. Regional cases and historical actors must not be collapsed into one borderland model.
